title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-06-24
lineage: Sony dynamic mics > Sony TC124; Tascam 122 MK-III > Lucid ADA1000 > Tascam CDRW 700 > Mac G4 Titanium Powerbook > Peak 3.2.1 > xACT V 1.2 > FLAC16

ai_review.summary: Stellar audience recording of the legendary 6/24/70 Capitol Theatre show – crystal‑clear crowd ambience captures a fire‑storm set highlighted by an epic Dark Star/Attics/Sugar Magnolia suite.
ai_review.review: The AUD tape, while not a soundboard, is remarkably clear and lets listeners feel the audience’s frenzy as much as the band’s playing. The performance itself is often called one of the greatest of 1970, with a monster Dark Star sequence, blistering Not Fade Away → Easy Wind, an early Sugar Magnolia, and a seamless St Stephen → China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider run that many fans cite as transcendent. Minor flaws include occasional drop‑outs and confusing disc ordering, but they hardly detract from the magic.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 40 reviews overwhelmingly praise both the musical performance (70% weight) and the surprisingly high‑quality audience recording (30% weight). Consistent five‑star ratings and repeated superlatives justify a near‑perfect score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear enough for most listeners; captures crowd reactions, occasional audience screams, and ambient room sound. Minor issues: some drop‑outs, a few tracks sound a bit muffled, and disc organization is confusing.

standout_songs: St. Stephen > China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
poor_songs: Early acoustic set (considered average by a few reviewers)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Shows a magical progression: early acoustic, New Riders sets, then an electric marathon that launches with Not Fade Away → Easy Wind and spirals into the legendary Dark Star/Attics/Sugar Magnolia suite, ending with high‑energy St. Stephen/China Cat/Rider and a heartfelt Swing Low, Sweet Chariot encore.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly described as 'smoking', 'transcendent' and delivering perfect guitar tones throughout the Dark Star saga.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for his deep, sustaining bass notes that anchor the jams; a few reviewers note his “bombs” during Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned for solid rhythm work and complementary lead lines, especially in the China Cat → Rider transition.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart lauded for a driving, manic percussion engine that propels Not Fade Away, Easy Wind and the Dark Star sections.
